output: {"answers":{"d03":"正反馈是输出的结果反过来加强输入，使变化沿原方向自我加速。麦克风靠近音箱：声音被拾入、放大、再播出、再被拾入，音量一圈比一圈大。机制是回路：变化→结果→结果进一步推动同一变化，每绕一圈都朝同方向加码，微小扰动被滚成雪球。但正反馈不判断好坏，只负责放大——放大什么才是关键。复利放大储蓄是好事；银行恐慌里『一挤兑就更恐慌、更恐慌就更多人挤兑』是灾难。判断依据：看回路放大的是期望的变化还是不想要的变化，以及有无刹车（资源耗尽、外部干预）。条件变化：若回路增益小于1，放大变成衰减，系统回归平稳。抢购潮与病毒传播是同一结构。","v02":"Search for 'jaguar' returns 10 results: 8 about the animal, 2 about cars; the corpus actually contains 20 animal pages. Precision = 8/10: of what was returned, how much is relevant — a quality check on the results shown. Recall = 8/20: of everything relevant that exists, how much was found — a coverage check. Same system, different questions. Change one condition: return all 20 animal pages plus the 2 car pages — recall is now 100%, precision drops to ~91%. Return just 1 certain hit — precision 100%, recall 5%. The two trade off, and which matters depends on the task: legal discovery tolerates junk but must not miss documents (recall); a results page users won't scroll past needs precision.","d06":"A cache keeps a copy of data close by so you don't refetch it every time — like keeping today's menu on a card instead of walking to the kitchen to ask. The problem: the kitchen changes the menu, your card goes stale, and you serve outdated answers. Cache invalidation is the rule deciding when a copy must be thrown away or refreshed. Example: a product page is cached for 5 minutes; the price changes in the database; until the copy expires or is deleted, users see the old price. Two strategies: expire after a fixed time (simple, but there's always a stale window) or actively delete the cache entry whenever the data is written (fresher, but every write path must remember to do it, and the delete can fail). Rarely-changing content suits a long timer; prices and inventory need short timers or active deletion. It's called a hard problem because correctness depends on catching every path that changes the data.","d02":"Two classes both average 70. One's scores all sit between 68 and 72; the other's run from 40 to 100. The average can't tell them apart — it says nothing about spread. Variance measures spread: the average of squared distances from the mean. For {40, 100, 60, 80}: deviations are −30, 30, −10, 10; squares are 900, 900, 100, 100; the average is 500. For {70, 70, 70, 70} it's 0. Why square? Distances above and below the mean would cancel to zero if merely summed; squaring makes them all count and, as a side effect, punishes big gaps far more than small ones. One wrinkle: the units become 'points squared', which is why people often take the square root (standard deviation) to get back to points. A single extreme score — say one 0 — inflates variance sharply because of that squaring.","v05":"信息熵衡量结果揭晓前你有多难猜：概率越分散，越没有可倚仗的倾向，熵越大。公式 H = −Σ p·log p：某个结果的 p 越小，log p 越负，它出现时越『惊讶』，熵就是平均惊讶度。均匀分布最不确定，因为没有任何结果可让你押注：两个结果各 50% 时 H = 1 比特；改成 99% 和 1%，几乎总是前者，H ≈ 0.08 比特——同样的两个选项，确定性天差地别。反过来看更清楚：只要概率不均匀，你就能偏向大概率结果来降低猜测难度，所以熵在均匀处取最大值。条件变化：均匀分布的选项从 2 个增到 8 个，H 从 1 升到 3 比特——依然均匀，但选择更多，同样更难猜。注意熵是整个概率分布的属性，不描述某一次具体结果。","d05":"某病患病率 1%，检测很准：病人 99% 呈阳性，健康人也有 5% 被误报。测出阳性，患病概率是 99% 吗？算一算 10 万人：1000 个病人里 990 人阳性；99000 个健康人里 4950 人被误报。阳性共 5940 人，其中真病人只占 990/5940 ≈ 16.7%。健康人基数太大，误报喧宾夺主。贝叶斯公式就是这个算法的一般化：P(病|阳性) = P(阳性|病)×P(病) ÷ P(阳性)，分子是『有病且检出』的人数占比，分母把所有阳性来源加总。关键是方向：P(阳性|病) 描述检测性能，P(病|阳性) 才是你要的答案，二者不是一回事。条件变化：换成患病率 10% 的高危人群，同样的检测，阳性中真病人比例升到约 68%——先验概率决定同样的证据把你推到哪儿。","v01":"Overfitting is memorizing instead of understanding. A student who memorizes every answer in the practice book — including its typos — aces that book but collapses on the real exam. A model overfits the same way: it treats noise and coincidences in its training data as patterns, performs superbly on data it has seen, and does worse on new data. How to tell it from the opposite problem: failing on both training and new data is underfitting — it never learned. Low error on training data but high error on new data is the overfitting signature. The mechanism: the more flexible the model, the more coincidence it can absorb; the less data, the more coincidence looks like a pattern. Remedies follow from that: more data, a simpler model, or stopping training earlier. The same shape appears elsewhere: a trading rule that 'explains' the past decade perfectly may just have memorized historical noise.","v08":"Little's law: L = λ × W. L is the average number of items in the system, λ the average arrival rate, W the average time an item spends in the system. Coffee shop: 10 customers arrive per minute, each spends 3 minutes from joining the line to leaving — so on average 30 people are inside. Why multiply: each arrival contributes 'one person present' for the duration of their stay, so head-count equals arrivals per minute times minutes of stay. The law lets you measure any two and compute the third: a server handling 1000 requests/s with 0.2 s each needs about 200 in flight. Conditions: steady state — averages stable, inflow roughly equals outflow. It assumes nothing about queue discipline or arrival distributions. Change one thing: cut service time to 0.1 s at the same arrival rate and the crowd halves to 100.","v07":"公共物品有两个特征：用不坏（我走路灯的光，不减少你的），挡不住（不交钱的人也照得见）。路灯、防洪堤、干净的空气都如此。搭便车正由此而生：既然享受无法排除，每个人最划算的做法就是不出钱，等别人付。例子：一栋楼十户，门禁系统共 1000 元，每户觉得安全值 200 元——对整栋楼明明划算。但装好后不交费的住户照样受益，于是每户都倾向少报自己的需要，结果可能是集体不装，尽管人人都想要。这解释了为什么这类东西市场往往供给不足，常要靠税收强制分摊。判断依据：先看是否『用不坏、挡不住』；电影院座位会被坐掉、能检票，就不算。条件变化：一旦技术能排除不付钱者（加密电视），搭便车被堵住，私人供给就变得可行。","v03":"自然选择改变的不是个体，而是种群中特征的频率。它不需要任何动物『努力』：长颈鹿的脖子不是伸出来的。机制分三步：同种个体存在可遗传的差异（脖子天生略长些）；差异影响存活和繁殖（高处有叶，略长者吃得多、留下的后代多）；后代继承这些差异，于是『长脖』在群体中的比例逐代升高。个体终生脖子不变，变的是下一代里哪种特征更常见——进化发生在群体层面。它也没有目的：选择只按当下环境淘汰，不管『未来用不用得上』。条件变化：若矮处食物同样充足，长脖优势消失，比例不再上升；环境反转甚至会反向淘汰。迁移：细菌耐药不是细菌努力变强，而是药水里恰好带耐药基因的少数个体存活并繁殖，把它们的频率顶了上去。","v04":"An operation is idempotent when doing it once and doing it many times leave the same result. Distributed systems care because networks fail awkwardly: you send a request, the connection drops, the server may have processed it, and you can't tell. So clients retry — and retrying a non-idempotent operation is dangerous: 'charge $100' sent twice is $200. The standard fix: the client attaches an idempotency key (a unique request ID); the server stores results by key and returns the stored result if the same key arrives again, making retries harmless. The identification test: does repeating change the end state? 'Set order status to shipped' — same state either way, idempotent. 'Add one item to cart' — one extra item, not. Condition change: if delivery were exactly-once you'd need none of this, but that guarantee is impractical over a network, so systems settle for at-least-once delivery plus idempotent handlers.","d01":"同一批数据，换不同假设去问『哪个假设让这批数据最可能出现』——这个可能性就是似然。抛硬币 10 次得 7 次正面：若硬币均匀（p=0.5），这结果出现的概率约 0.117；若 p=0.7，约 0.267。0.267 就是『p=0.7 时数据的概率』；固定数据、比较假设，似然才有意义。后验回答的是反方向的问题：『看到这 7 正 3 反之后，硬币 p=0.7 的可信度多大？』由贝叶斯公式，后验 ∝ 似然 × 先验。两者方向相反：似然是『假设→数据』的概率，不是『数据→假设』的概率。所以说『似然 0.267，说明 p=0.7 有 26.7% 的可能』是错的——那是后验才回答的事，而且还要看先验和其他 p 值的似然。一句话：似然用来比较假设，后验给假设打分。","v06":"Two processes, two files. Process A has locked file 1 and now wants file 2. Process B has locked file 2 and wants file 1. Each will only release its lock after finishing, and finishing requires the other's lock — so both wait forever. That's deadlock: a cycle of waiting where everyone holds something someone else needs. Four conditions must hold simultaneously: resources are exclusive, holders keep them while waiting, nothing can be taken by force, and the waits form a circle. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible — in practice the easiest is the circle: agree that everyone acquires file 1 before file 2, and A and B can no longer cycle. Condition change: if B gives up and releases file 2 after a timeout, the cycle breaks and work resumes. The same shape appears in databases, where two transactions lock rows in opposite orders.","d08":"Compound growth pays interest on interest. $1000 at 10%: after one year $1100, after two $1210 — the extra $10 is interest earned by the first year's interest — after three $1331. Formula: final = start × (1 + rate)^years. The exponent is the whole story: each year multiplies the running total instead of adding a fixed amount, so growth accelerates. A handy check: money doubles in roughly 72/rate% years — at 10%, about 7. Why the starting amount matters: it's the base being multiplied. $1000 and $2000, same 10%, same 30 years, become $17,449 and $34,898 — double the start, double the result, because the gap itself compounds. Condition change: drop the rate to 5% and $1000 over 30 years yields only $4,322; with time sitting in the exponent, the rate's effect is enormous. The same math runs debt, population growth, and epidemics — compounding works in both directions.","d04":"You have a free afternoon. Options: nap, see a movie with a friend, or take a freelance gig worth $200. Whatever you pick, the afternoon is spent — so nothing here is literally free. Opportunity cost is the value of the single best option you gave up. Choose the movie: your cost isn't the nap plus the gig, just the $200 gig, because that was the best alternative — the nap loses to the gig, so it doesn't count. Choose the gig: your cost is the movie's enjoyment, whatever that's worth to you. The test for any 'free' choice: what would I otherwise do with this resource? Condition change: if the gig pays $1000, the movie becomes dramatically more expensive — many people's decision flips, which is exactly what rising wages do to leisure. Cost is always measured against the best forgone use, never the sum of all of them.","d07":"冰淇淋销量与溺水人数同涨同跌，相关很强，但吃冰淇淋不会让人溺水——背后有个共同原因：夏天高温，既让冰淇淋好卖，也让更多人下水。只比较同样炎热的日子，这层相关会明显减弱，说明它多半是共因投下的影子。反过来，吸烟与肺癌：控制住年龄、职业等因素后相关依然存在，加上动物实验给出机制，因果才被逐步确立。混淆有三种形状：A 导致 B；共因 C 同时推动 A 和 B；甚至方向相反。检验办法是干预：如果真是因果，改变 A 应该改变 B——戒烟后肺癌率下降支持因果；多关几家冰淇淋店，溺水不会减少，因果解读就此被戳破。相关是寻找因果的线索，但要有额外证据——机制、对照、干预——才能把相关坐实为因果。"}}
